newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo backtracks on Russian pilot ban.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo backtracks on Russian pilot ban.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's government on Wednesday backtracked on a ban on Russian pilots and Russian-made aircraft in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Transport Minister Henri Mova told Reuters that those who conformed to international standards could continue operating.
"Up until now, no plane has been banned from operating. Many pilots don't fulfil the necessary flying conditions. But no decision has been made yet in this regard," he said.

Mova told state television at the weekend that he had banned the use by local airlines of Russian pilots or Russian-made planes and complained about their qualifications and lack of knowledge about the condition of the planes.
"We've noticed that most of the aircraft which are in good condition are Russian-made. So we've nothing against them," he said on Wednesday.

He acknowledged that many of the 220 planes operating in the former Zaire could not been allowed to fly. He said the government would clamp down on air companies which did not abide by the country's legislation.

The New Congo has about a hundred private air companies. Many used to bribe the officials under former president Mobutu Sese Seko, who was ousted by Kabila's forces in May. Corrupt officials turned a blind eye to the carriers' activities.
A Russian-piloted Antonov crashed on a market place on take-off in Kinshasa in 1996 killing at least 330 people. An inquiry blamed overloading and human error.
